question: If mean, median, and mode of a moderately skewed observations are (x - 1), (2x - 4) and '2x', respectively, then find the value of 'x'.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Empirical relation: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

2x = 3(2x − 4) − 2(x − 1)

2x = 6x − 12 − 2x + 2

2x = 4x − 10 ⇒ 2x = 10 ⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean = (x − 1)

Median = (2x − 4)

Mode = 2x

**Formula Used:**

For a moderately skewed distribution: Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean)

 
• Mean x − 1 Median 2x − 4 Mode 2x Empirical Relationship Scale 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ 2x = 3(2x − 4) − 2(x − 1)

⇒ 2x = 6x − 12 − 2x + 2

⇒ 2x = (6x − 2x) − (12 − 2)

⇒ 2x = 4x − 10

⇒ 10 = 4x − 2x

⇒ 10 = 2x

⇒ x = 10 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

In a moderately skewed distribution, the distance between the mean and the median is about one-third of the distance between the mean and the mode.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, Mean = Median = Mode. Any deviation from this equality indicates skewness.

Types of Skewness

If Mean > Median > Mode, it is positively skewed. If Mode > Median > Mean, it is negatively skewed.
